clue.text: A lake's in the region providing water

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces sit inside the word for region

parts.note: a region is an area
L is the map abbreviation for lake, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A geography note about a lake that supplies water to the surrounding district.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aral Sea, in Central Asia, is in fact a lake despite its name, which makes 'A lake' a neat touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea is a body of water, loosely described here as something that provides water.

clue.text: Soldier arising in a halo of stars

indicators.note: in tells us the soldier sits inside the halo word

parts.note: an aura is a halo of light

indicators.note: arising in a down clue tells us the letters read upwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier emerging within a glowing ring of stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Auriga, the Charioteer, is a northern constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Keen to get skill without study

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside tells us the skill word wraps round the study

parts.note: art is a skill or craft
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Eager to gain an ability without doing any learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like an omission signal, but here it carries its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate and eager, a direct synonym for keen.

clue.text: Killjoy prizes wine

parts.note: spoils are prizes or booty
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A grump who wins drink as a reward.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport is someone who ruins others' fun, an exact synonym for killjoy.

clue.text: Trembling like a bird

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Shaking in the manner of a frightened bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is the trembling poplar, and aspen as an adjective means quivering.

clue.text: Pick a president in time

parts.note: a point is a moment or particular time

explanation.surface: Choosing someone to lead a country at the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here, joining the pieces to the time word.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick someone for a post is to name or nominate them to it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Ill man ate stew that's nutritious

indicators.note: stew tells us the letters are cooked up and mixed together

explanation.surface: A sick man ate some stew, which was nourishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimental means relating to food or nourishment, hence nutritious.

clue.text: Mean to consume English fruit

indicators.note: to consume tells us the average word swallows the English letter

parts.note: par is the average or mean

explanation.surface: A stingy person eating an English fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like stingy but is the average, PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a common orchard fruit, a definition by example.

clue.text: Lazy old Liberal detained by order

indicators.note: detained by tells us the two letters are held inside the order word

parts.note: an indent is an official order for goods

explanation.surface: An idle old politician held in custody by command.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolent means habitually idle, a direct synonym for lazy.

clue.text: Salt for strumpet's roast

parts.note: a strumpet is a prostitute, a tart
to rate is to scold severely, as to roast someone

explanation.surface: A dish of salt meat cooked for a woman of ill repute.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartrate is a salt of tartaric acid, chemical salts being the sense meant.

clue.text: Moved round cattle pen

parts.note: rode means travelled or moved on horseback
O is a round shape

explanation.surface: Animals shifted around an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America a rodeo is also the enclosure where cattle are rounded up, a less familiar sense.

clue.text: Briefly, prince and queen play around

indicators.note: briefly asks for the name cut short to its familiar shortened form

parts.note: Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A gossip column hinting that royals have been having affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims PHILIP to the nickname PHIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to have casual affairs, which is what to play around means idiomatically.

clue.text: Armed man turns friendly? Stick around!

indicators.note: turns tells us the word for friendly is read backwards

parts.note: snug can mean cosy and intimate, close and friendly
to stick around is to linger

explanation.surface: A man with a weapon suddenly becomes amiable and invites you to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunslinger is a gunman of the Wild West, someone carrying a weapon.

clue.text: To drink loudly, not quietly, is an insult

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for quietly is left out

parts.note: to slurp is to drink noisily
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Noisy drinking is rude, unlike sipping quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is a disparaging remark, a direct synonym for an insult.

clue.text: Greg 'ad a VAT mix-up that made matters worse

indicators.note: mix-up tells us the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Greg's tax muddle only worsened things.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggravated means made a problem or situation more serious, so made matters worse.

clue.text: Found a predator like Richard III

parts.note: to found an institution is to plant or establish it
a genet is a small, cat-like carnivore of Africa and Europe

explanation.surface: Discovering a hunting animal that resembles a notorious king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' reads as the past tense of find, but it means establish.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard III was the last king of the royal house named here, so it describes him as an adjective.

clue.text: Lamenting bad association

indicators.note: bad tells us the letters are in poor order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Grieving over a poor partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: An alignment is an alliance or grouping, so a form of association.

clue.text: Bottle for sailors in bar

indicators.note: in tells us the sailors go inside the bar word

parts.note: to bar is to stop
a crew is a body of sailors

explanation.surface: A bottle for seamen in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but means block.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwtop is a bottle with a screw cap, so the container is named by its closure.

clue.text: Switch on the kettle for top performer

parts.note: to start a machine is to switch it on
an urn is a large kettle for making tea

explanation.surface: Putting the kettle on for the headline act.
explanation.walkthrough: A star turn is British theatre slang for the main act on a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A star turn is the leading act of a show, the top performer.

clue.text: Supply support vehicle

parts.note: to cater is to supply food
a pillar is a supporting column

explanation.surface: Providing backup transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caterpillar is a tracked tractor or crawler vehicle, named after the trade mark.

clue.text: Satisfy parking agreement

parts.note: P is the symbol for parking
a lease is a rental agreement

explanation.surface: Meeting needs with a contract for a parking space.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to satisfy or gratify them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Always in the right to go back

indicators.note: in tells us the always word sits inside the right abbreviation

parts.note: RT is short for right
ever means always

explanation.surface: Being permanently correct about returning.
explanation.definitionFit: To revert is to return to an earlier state, a synonym of go back.

clue.text: Notice bridge player's merit

parts.note: to give ear is to notice or heed, so ear means attention
N is North, one of the four players at a bridge table

explanation.surface: Spotting the skill of a card player.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to earn it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Think little of foreign articles Glen holds superior

parts.note: un is a French indefinite article
der is a German definite article

indicators.note: holds tells us the valley word contains the letter for superior

parts.note: a glen is a valley, or vale
U stands for upper class, socially superior

explanation.surface: Disparaging imported goods while a Scottish valley is rated higher.
explanation.definitionFit: To undervalue is to underrate, which is to think little of something.

clue.text: Workman disregards quibble to sign up

indicators.note: disregards tells us the quibble word is ignored and taken away

parts.note: a carpenter is a workman in wood
to carp is to quibble

explanation.surface: A builder ignores petty objections when enrolling.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a competition is to sign up for it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Make better pickle

definitions.meaning: to preserve meat or fish by salting or smoking

explanation.definitionFit: Curing heals an illness, and curing also preserves food such as bacon or herring.

clue.text: It's said the merchandise you supplied is contentious

indicators.note: it's said tells us the phrase is spoken to make the answer

parts.note: truck is an old word for goods or merchandise, and 'you lent' is what you supplied

explanation.surface: A complaint that the goods someone provided are causing argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Truck in the sense of commodities survives in the phrase 'have no truck with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Truculent means aggressively defiant and quarrelsome, so a close synonym for contentious.

clue.text: Fly back with oriental deal

indicators.note: back tells us the word for fly is read in reverse

parts.note: to dart is to fly swiftly
E is East, oriental meaning eastern

explanation.surface: Flying home with an Eastern business arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade is to deal in goods, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Sarcastic quip by toff

parts.note: a pun is a witty play on words
a toff is a posh gentleman, a gent

explanation.surface: A biting witticism from an upper-class man.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent remarks are sharp and caustic, which matches sarcastic.

clue.text: Dear me! Tory leader upset food

indicators.note: upset tells us the letters are knocked over and rearranged
leader picks out the opening letter of Tory

explanation.surface: An exclamation of dismay that the head of the Conservatives has been knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: Red meat such as beef or lamb is a kind of food, so this is a definition by example.
